title: Implementing Detection as Code as a multi-platform MSSP
content_md: What was once considered to be a niche within a niche, Detection as Code has become a very popular method of managing detection rules across your SIEM environment. Seeing Detection as Code pipelines become commonplace has been incredibly heartening to watch over the last few years, as it brings with it very tangible benefits — removes the risk of configuration drift, allows for unit testing and strict style guides through CI/CD, and automated deployments. With AI in the picture, the benefits multiply massively with huge efficiency boosts in terms of writing and tuning rules, using those rules for threat hunting, and more. I’ve spent a long time tracking the evolution of Detection as Code in the Detection Engineering space in my last few years as a security engineer at an MSSP. I tried many different approaches to implementing DaC in a way that could truly scale, and scale in a way that could function cross-platform, as we support not one but four platforms simultaneously! I found very online discussing how they were dealing with the complexities that arise from dealing with this large of an environment. This article intends to address this use-case. First and foremost, a lot of the initial inspiration came from the incredible work done by NVISO Labs on their Detection Engineering: Practicing Detection-as-Code — NVISO Labs series of blogs.
